response.report:
EXAM: Chest radiograph, one view, 2026-11-12
CLINICAL INDICATION: Routine surveillance. History of treated breast cancer. No new symptoms.
ORDERING PROVIDER: Dr. L. Okafor (synthetic), medical oncology
COMPARISON: Chest radiograph, 2026-02-10
TECHNIQUE: Current PA. Prior PA. Same view on both studies, no contrast. Differences from prior: current has slightly deeper inspiration, slightly greater penetration and contrast, and different shoulder, arm and breast position. Comparison is possible. Both image files are downsampled, which limits fine detail.

LOOK AT FIRST:
- F2: Small dense nodular focus with mildly prominent linear markings in the medial right lower zone. It is not clearly seen on the prior. Both reads called it indeterminate. Not flagged time-sensitive and no on-call page triggered, but triage urgency is high because of the surveillance history. Radiologist review of the source images is needed early.
- F1: Left chest venous access port and catheter. Catheter tip not traced. The two reads disagreed (one stable, one indeterminate), so it is indeterminate.

FINDINGS (systematic read, done blind to the indication):
- Airway / lungs: Trachea central, no narrowing seen. Lungs well expanded. No consolidation, mass or collapse. Left lung clear. Apices clear. Right lower zone: mildly prominent linear bronchovascular markings in the medial zone, with a single small dense nodular focus projected among them (F2). Status indeterminate; both reads indeterminate. The markings are more conspicuous than on the prior, and the nodular focus is not clearly seen on the prior. The current study is slightly more penetrated with higher contrast, which might explain the appearance. No confluent consolidation.
- Mediastinum / hila: Prominent rounded aortic knuckle, consistent with an unfolded aorta (F3), with the same contour and prominence on the prior. Upper mediastinum not widened. Hila normal in position, with no one-sided hilar enlargement.
- Pleura: No pleural line to suggest pneumothorax. Both costophrenic angles sharp on the current study. No pleural thickening. On the prior, the left costophrenic angle was overlapped by breast shadow without definite blunting.
- Heart: Cardiac silhouette not enlarged on either PA film (F4, recorded by one of the two reads). Borders distinct. Heart width is slightly smaller on the current, in keeping with slightly deeper inspiration. No change in size or contour.
- Bones / soft tissue: No rib, clavicle or shoulder fracture or destructive lesion seen at this resolution. Mild curvature of the thoracic spine, similar on both films (F5, recorded by one of the two reads). Bilateral breast shadows overlie the lower zones. No soft tissue gas. Device (F1): thin tubing arcs across the left upper zone from the medial left clavicular region to a small metallic component, consistent with an implanted venous access port and catheter. Same configuration on both studies, no kink or discontinuity seen at this resolution. It projects higher on the current. Catheter tip not traced. Status indeterminate; the two reads disagreed (read A stable, read B indeterminate). Upper abdomen on the frontal view: both domes well defined, gastric bubble and gas-filled bowel loops under the left dome, no free gas under the diaphragm.

INTERVAL CHANGE:
- Changed: No definite interval change established. The right lower zone markings and small dense focus (F2) look more conspicuous on the current, but this is indeterminate because of the exposure and contrast difference. The left chest port projects higher on the current (F1). Whether this is true migration or positional difference from arm and breast position is indeterminate, and the reads disagreed. No measurements are available.
- Unchanged: Aortic knuckle prominence and mediastinal contour are similar. Hila are similar. Cardiac silhouette is not enlarged and is similar. No pneumothorax on either study. Spinal alignment is similar. Device configuration is the same, with no new device.

RECIST 1.1: not computed on radiographs

CAN'T DETERMINE:
- Is the small dense focus in the medial right lower zone a true lung nodule, and is it new? | Reason: The focus is small and lies among vessels, so a vessel seen end-on or a calcified granuloma cannot be separated from a nodule on a frontal film. The softer exposure of the prior may hide it. | Recommend: Review the source images in PACS. If it persists, CT chest.
- Have the right lower zone lung markings truly increased since the prior? | Reason: The current study is more penetrated with higher contrast, which makes fine markings more conspicuous without a real change. | Recommend: Review source images side by side in PACS with matched windowing. Interval follow-up PA film, or CT chest if there is clinical concern.
- Where is the tip of the left-sided venous catheter? | Reason: The thin catheter cannot be followed over the dense mediastinal shadow on these low-resolution frontal images. | Recommend: Review the source image in PACS with edge-enhanced windowing, or obtain a lateral view.
- Where is the tip of the left-sided venous catheter, and has it moved? | Reason: The catheter is lost over the dense mediastinal shadow on both films at this resolution. The chest wall component projects at a different rib level on the two films. | Recommend: Review the source images in PACS with window adjustment. Add a lateral view if tip position matters clinically.
- Is the tiny dense focus over the right lower zone on current a nodule, a vessel end-on or a calcified granuloma, and is it new? | Reason: The focus is too small for a frontal X-ray to separate a nodule from a vessel end-on or a bone island. On the prior the same area is covered by breast shadow on a lower contrast film. | Recommend: Review the source image in PACS. CT chest if it persists or is of clinical concern.
- Are the more conspicuous right lower zone markings on current a real interval change? | Reason: Breast shadow overlap, contrast and depth of inspiration differ between the two films. | Recommend: Correlate clinically. Repeat PA and lateral with matched technique, or CT chest if concern persists.
- Are the faint linear densities lateral to the left hilum on prior a real band of atelectasis or scarring, and have they cleared? | Reason: Mild rotation and lower contrast on prior. Vessels and the overlying catheter cross the same area. The appearance is not reproduced on current. | Recommend: Review the source images in PACS. No further imaging needed if the radiologist confirms normal vessels.
- Is there a subtle rib, spine or shoulder lesion? | Reason: The low resolution, compressed image limits fine bone detail. Shoulders and ribs are partly overlapped by soft tissue. | Recommend: Review the source images in PACS on bone settings. Dedicated imaging if there is focal pain or clinical concern.

IMPRESSION:
1. Indeterminate small dense nodular focus with mildly prominent linear markings in the medial right lower zone (F2). It is not clearly seen on the prior, and both reads were indeterminate. Whether it is a true nodule, and whether it is new, cannot be determined on these films. Differences in exposure and contrast might account for the appearance. Given the history of treated breast cancer, early radiologist review of the source images is advised.
2. Left chest implanted venous access port and catheter (F1), indeterminate. The reads disagreed. It projects higher than on the prior, which may be positional. The catheter tip is not traced.
3. Otherwise, at this resolution there is no mass, pleural effusion, hilar or mediastinal enlargement, destructive bone lesion or pneumothorax. The cardiac silhouette is not enlarged. The aortic knuckle is prominent and similar to the prior.
4. Several questions remain open, including the faint left perihilar linear densities on the prior and subtle bone lesions. See CAN'T DETERMINE.

RECOMMENDATIONS:
- Review the source images in PACS with matched windowing, side by side with the prior, for the right lower zone focus and markings (F2).
- CT chest if the right lower zone focus persists on source image review or if there is clinical concern. No interval was specified in the findings.
- Interval follow-up PA film, or repeat PA and lateral with matched technique, if the markings remain uncertain. No interval was specified in the findings.
- Lateral view or edge-enhanced PACS review for the catheter tip if tip position matters clinically (F1).

AI DRAFT: requires resident review and attending signature.
